# pylaag

> pylaag is a Python library collection for reading, writing, and manipulating API specification formats. It is the Python port of the [laag](https://github.com/bschwarz/laag) TypeScript library, providing equivalent functionality with idiomatic Python APIs.

## Packages

- `pylaag-openapi` — Read and write OpenAPI 3.0+ documents, validate specs, generate sample data, client code (Python/JS/TS), and curl commands
- `pylaag-smithy` — Parse and manipulate AWS Smithy 2.0 models (JSON AST format)
- `pylaag-raml` — RAML support (in development)
- `pylaag-core` — Abstract base class (`LaagBase`) and shared errors used by all packages

## Installation

```bash
pip install pylaag-openapi pylaag-smithy
```

## @pylaag/openapi — OpenAPIDocument + manager classes

```python
from pylaag.openapi import (
    OpenAPIDocument, PathManager, HttpMethod,
    ComponentManager, ComponentType,
    SampleGenerator, CodeGenerator, Language, CurlGenerator,
)

# Create / parse
doc = OpenAPIDocument()                          # empty doc with defaults
doc = OpenAPIDocument({"openapi": "3.0.0", ...})
doc = OpenAPIDocument.from_json(json_str)
doc = OpenAPIDocument.from_yaml(yaml_str)

# Properties
doc.openapi_version    # "3.0.0"
doc.info               # {"title": ..., "version": ...}
doc.paths              # {"paths": {...}}

# Serialize
doc.to_json(indent=2)  # JSON string
doc.to_yaml()          # YAML string

# Validate (raises ValidationError if invalid)
doc.validate()

# PathManager
path_mgr = PathManager(doc)
path_mgr.add_path("/users")
path_mgr.add_operation("/users", "get", {"summary": "...", "responses": {...}})
path_mgr.get_operation("/users", "get")    # dict | None
path_mgr.get_path("/users")               # dict | None
path_mgr.remove_operation("/users", "get") # bool
path_mgr.remove_path("/users")             # bool

# ComponentManager
comp_mgr = ComponentManager(doc)
comp_mgr.add_component("schemas", "User", {"type": "object", "properties": {...}})
comp_mgr.get_component("schemas", "User")     # dict | None
comp_mgr.remove_component("schemas", "User")  # bool
comp_mgr.resolve_reference("#/components/schemas/User")  # dict | None

# SampleGenerator
gen = SampleGenerator(doc)
gen.generate_from_schema(schema_dict)  # returns sample value

# CurlGenerator
curl_gen = CurlGenerator(doc)
curl_gen.generate_curl("/users", "post", base_url="https://api.example.com")
# raises NotFoundError if operation missing

# CodeGenerator
codegen = CodeGenerator(doc)
codegen.generate_client("python")      # Python requests client
codegen.generate_client("javascript")  # JS fetch client
codegen.generate_client("typescript")  # TS fetch client
```

## @pylaag/smithy — SmithyDocument + manager classes

```python
from pylaag.smithy import SmithyDocument, ShapeManager, TraitManager, OperationManager

# Create / parse
doc = SmithyDocument()
doc = SmithyDocument({"smithy": "2.0", "shapes": {}})
doc = SmithyDocument.from_json(json_str)

# Properties
doc.smithy_version  # "2.0"
doc.shapes          # dict[str, Any]

# Serialize & validate
doc.to_json(indent=2)
doc.validate()  # raises ValidationError if missing required fields

# ShapeManager
shape_mgr = ShapeManager(doc)
shape_mgr.add_shape("com.example#User", "structure", {"members": {...}})
shape_mgr.get_shape("com.example#User")       # dict | None
shape_mgr.resolve_target("com.example#User")  # dict | None
shape_mgr.remove_shape("com.example#User")    # bool

# Shape types: "service" | "operation" | "resource" | "structure" | "union" |
#              "list" | "map" | "string" | "integer" | "long" | "float" |
#              "double" | "boolean" | "blob" | "timestamp"

# TraitManager
trait_mgr = TraitManager(doc)
trait_mgr.add_trait_to_shape("com.example#GetUser", "smithy.api#readonly")
trait_mgr.add_trait_to_shape("com.example#GetUser", "smithy.api#http", {"method": "GET", "uri": "/users/{id}"})
trait_mgr.get_trait("com.example#GetUser", "smithy.api#http")  # Any | None
trait_mgr.remove_trait_from_shape("com.example#GetUser", "smithy.api#http")  # bool
# raises NotFoundError if shape doesn't exist
```

## @pylaag/core — LaagBase, errors

```python
from pylaag.core import LaagBase, ParseError, ValidationError, NotFoundError

# All packages' document classes extend LaagBase.
# ParseError    — raised when JSON/YAML cannot be parsed
# ValidationError — raised on invalid document structure
# NotFoundError   — raised when a referenced resource doesn't exist
```
